Q: Per-element atomicity of vector load/store and gather/scatter? A:

As of 2026, part of the answer changed after this question was asked back than in 2017.

Intel now guarantees atomic aligned 16-byte memory operations on processors which enumerate AVX, but only for legacy MOVAPD/MOVAPS/MOVDQA, their VEX.128 forms, and their EVEX.128 forms with k0 (masking disabled). The exact SDM wording is quoted in GCC's libatomic patch. AMD likewise extends atomicity a cacheable, naturally aligned single load or store from 8 to 16 bytes when AVX is reported; see section 7.3.2 of AMD APM Volume 2.

Thus those plain aligned 128-bit moves are atomic as a whole and therefore per element. No correspodning gaurantee is stated for 256- or 512-bit moves.

The answer remains no documented guarantee for masked moves. The elementwise Load_32/Load_64 pseudocode is functional notation, not a promise about memory-transaction granularity. Intel even calls the access and ordering of VMASKMOV implementation-specific for MMIO and uncached memory; VPMASKMOV omits "the access and", but in my opinion that difference is too weak and context-specific to establish per-element atomicity for cacheable memory.

The current gather documentation is clearer than it was in 2017. VPGATHERDD/QD epxlicitly warns that implementations may use loads larger than the element size or load an element more than once. Therefore FETCH_32BITS does not establish a separate 32-bit transaction. "Follows the Intel-64 memory-ordering model" orders whatever accesses the implementation pefrorms; it does not define their width or grant each pseudocode element atomicity. VPSCATTER also gives ordering and restart rules, but no per-element atomicity guarantee.

So the manual-based answer is: yes for the documented aligned 128-bit plain moves; not documented for masked moves, gathers, scatters, or 256-/512-bit moves. Current hardware may be stronger: testing on Skylake and Zen 2 found aligned 128- and 256-bit VMOVDQA atomic, but that is empirical evidence rather than an architectural promise.

This conclusion addresses only hardware. In ISO C or C++, accessing atomic<int32_t> objects thruogh non-atomic SIMD operations still has language-level data-race and compiler-semantics problems.

Q: How to use Flutter on a Linux Mint computer with a physical phone A:

Yes, you can run a Flutter app directly on a physical Android phone without using an emulator. 👍

You don't need Android Studio to actually run the app on the phone, although you still need the Flutter SDK and Android SDK/tooling.

On your phone:

  1. Enable Developer options.

  2. Enable USB debugging.

  3. Connect the phone to your Linux Mint PC with a USB cable.

  4. Accept the USB debugging authorization prompt on the phone.

  5. In the terminal, run:

flutter devices

Your phone should appear in the device list. Then run:

flutter run

If Flutter doesn't detect the phone, check:

adb devices

On Linux, you may also need the appropriate ADB/udev permissions for your phone.

Since your computer only has 4 GB RAM, using a physical phone is actually a good approach because you can avoid the overhead of running an Android emulator. 🚀

Q: How to fix executor failed running [/bin/sh -c pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall pip==9.0.3 && pip install --upgrade 'setuptools<45']: A:

I had the same issue, the problem was the base image I was using. Once I changed it to a working one the error disappeared. I specifically used a python3.9.10-slim image from our local repo. Once I switched to the regular python3.9.0 image all worked well.

The python3.9.10-slim image being corrupted is a problem in our repo but maybe what you're experiencing is caused by the same type of issue.

Q: List the details of employee ,department with a reference column A:

If query should ignore extra additional employees beyond count of n for each department, then Try this:

 with DeptEmps (deptId, empSequence) As
   (Select deptId, DeptReference
    From Departments d 
    union all
    Select deptId, empSequence - 1 
    From DeptEmps 
    Where empSequence > 1)

 Select d.DeptId, DeptName, 
    EmpId, EmpName, Salary
 From Departments d
    join DeptEmps de 
       on de.deptId = d.DeptId
   Left Join Employees e
       on e.DeptId = d.DeptId
          And de.empSequence =
            (Select Count(*)
             From Employees
             Where DeptId = e.DeptId
                and EmpId <= e.EmpId)
  Order By d.Deptname

If query should include extra additional employees beyond count of n for each department, then it gets a bit more complex: 

with DeptEmps (deptId, empSequence) As
  (Select deptId, 
      Case When d.DeptReference > 
          (Select Count(*) From Employees 
           Where DeptId = d.DeptId) Then d.DeptReference
   Else  (Select Count(*) From Employees 
              Where DeptId = d.DeptId) End empSequence  
   From Depts d 
      union all
   Select deptId, empSequence - 1 
   From DeptEmps 
   Where empSequence > 1)
Select  d.DeptId, DeptName, 
   EmpId, EmpName, Salary
From Depts d
   join DeptEmps de 
      on de.deptId = d.DeptId
   left Join Employees e
     on e.DeptId = de.DeptId
        And (Select Count(*)
             From Employees
             Where DeptId = e.DeptId
                and EmpId <= e.EmpId)
         = de.empSequence          
Order By d.Deptname
